rule: When stories write sibling reference files in parallel, split.md pins each shared contract (helper names and import paths, gate order, linter, canonical layout) in one owning file; others link it, and a fix to one greps every sibling.
why: Ten topic files shipped one session helper at four import paths, two gate orders and conflicting lint/middleware rules (R1-B15, R1-C9, R1-A5, R1-C6); FIX1 still left TEST-37 on the old gate order (R2-A3/R2-C1).
evidence: bmn.json assumptions: FIX1 session-helper contract decided after review

rule: Every 'Do' snippet in a references/nextjs topic obeys the standard's own rules: auth plus Origin check in each mutation, no side effect on GET, ApiErrorBody errors, every import present; the topic test checks Do fences against them.
why: Do blocks shipped unauthenticated Server Actions and POSTs, a mutating GET, missing node:crypto/ApiErrorBody imports and ad-hoc error bodies, against NN-3/API-13/API-17 (R1-A10, R1-B1, R1-B5, R1-B6, R1-B9, R2-B6, R2-C3).

rule: A regression guard a fixer adds must be shown to fail: revert only the fix and confirm the guard goes red, and feed it each variant of the bug (inline forms, look-alike names); a regex guard that passes on the old code is not a test.
why: FIX1 guards could not fail: removing both 'as Route' casts still passed 21/21, BARE_RETURN missed the inline return, and any verify-prefixed call satisfied the webhook guard (R2-A7, R2-B9, R2-B10).

rule: Run each review beside its test run, not after it, and merge every fixer's branch the moment it pushes; never hold a serial merge pass until all fixers are done.
why: REVIEW1 started only after TEST1 merged, and the ten FIX1 branches, all pushed by 05:33, merged one by one until 06:17; Jonathan asked why the run was slow, and only then did TEST2 and REVIEW2 run in parallel.
